records.scope: Classical probability-space/null-set background needed to state effective tests; computable measures; effective open sets; integral-test formulations.
records.why_it_matters: Test-based randomness definitions depend on exactly which null sets/measures/tests are effectively present.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S005 now has exact primary definitions for computable metric spaces, computable probability measures, computable probability spaces, effective-open/integral tests and arbitrary-measure uniform tests.

The inspected general-space framework is computable-metric-space based. Arbitrary represented-space probability formalisms were not separately primary-inspected, and classical measure theory beyond randomness-relevant machinery remains outside scope.
next_actions: Later close remaining foundational gaps only where they affect randomness definitions or theorem hypotheses; do not expand into a general computable-analysis survey.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: General computable metric/probability-space machinery and exact generalized ML/Schnorr resources are statement-grounded. Arbitrary represented-space probability formalisms are outside the depth required for discovery.

records.area: Historical statistical randomness, normality, von Mises and Church selection
records.scope: Normal numbers/statistical frequency tests; collectives; admissible place selections; Church effectivization; later stochasticity terminology.
records.why_it_matters: Separates frequency/selection approaches from stronger effective-test and betting notions and prevents ahistorical equivalence claims.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Borel and von Mises original sources not yet catalogued directly; Church source statement inspected; later terminology crosswalk incomplete.
next_actions: Add primary Borel/von Mises records and source-supported relationships among normality, Church stochasticity and modern notions.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Church's effective selection formulation is statement-inspected and the historical/statistical territory is navigable. Direct Borel/von Mises originals and a fuller terminology crosswalk would improve provenance but are not needed for Gate 1.

records.area: Martin-Löf randomness and effective null tests
records.scope: Core definitions, universal tests, equivalent formulations and foundational history for individual infinite sequences.
records.why_it_matters: Central benchmark notion against which many weaker, stronger, relative and generalized notions are calibrated.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S011 recovered and statement-inspected the original 1966 Martin-Löf article through a UCI-hosted full scan, with publication identity/DOI independently verified. The catalogue now preserves its exact nested/extension-closed sequential-test syntax, universal significance-level shift, finite-critical-level definition, maximal constructive-null-set reformulation, and separate arbitrary-computable-distribution extension.

Solovay's 1975 manuscript remains uninspected. Exact ordinary Solovay-test and c.e.-martingale characterizations are therefore grounded in later statement-inspected primary SRC-0059; direct original Solovay priority/detail is not reconstructed from citation trails.

Schnorr's 1973 Process Complexity and Effective Random Tests was located bibliographically/open-archive at publisher level during P1-S011, but direct full-statement retrieval through the available route was not reliable enough for promotion. The existing prefix-free incompressibility theorem is instead grounded in statement-inspected primary SRC-0045/SRC-0047 plus the established survey cross-check; earliest Levin/Schnorr priority is not re-adjudicated here.

The martingale characterization added in P1-S011 is the fair-coin c.e./lower-semicomputable martingale form explicitly stated in SRC-0059. No arbitrary-measure, oracle-relative or supermartingale generalization is inferred.
next_actions: If a reliable copy of the original Solovay draft or Schnorr 1973 internal statements becomes available, inspect it to close the remaining provenance gaps; otherwise preserve the present later-primary exact formulations.
Do not broaden COV-0003 by analogy into generalized measures, relativization, stronger tests or resource-bounded betting; those remain in their existing dedicated records.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Martin-Löf 1966 is statement-inspected; exact Solovay-test and c.e.-martingale characterizations are grounded in later primary literature. The uninspected Solovay draft and Schnorr 1973 internals are historical/provenance gaps, not dependencies of current theorem syntax.

records.area: Schnorr, computable, Kurtz and weak randomness notions
records.scope: Major weaker notions; exact test/betting resources; strictness and separation theorems; weak-n hierarchy where relevant.
records.why_it_matters: These notions expose how changes in effectivity/resource constraints alter randomness and provide a calibrated local landscape around Martin-Löf randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Schnorr's original 1971 book and unified article remain METADATA_ONLY internally; Kurtz's 1981 thesis remains METADATA_ONLY.

P1-S003 now has statement-level ordinary oracle formulations for computable, Schnorr and Kurtz randomness plus uniform-relative Schnorr/computable formulations, but generalized-measure versions are not normalized here.
Ordinary and uniformly relative Schnorr/computable randomness are deliberately not collapsed; van-Lambalgen behavior depends on this distinction.
next_actions: If accessible, close the original Schnorr/Kurtz internal-statement gap; otherwise preserve it.
Connect weaker notions to generalized computable measures/spaces in a later bounded session without importing fair-coin conventions by analogy.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Core weaker notions and strictness relations are statement-grounded in later primary papers. Original Schnorr/Kurtz internals remain useful historical retrieval targets but exact catalogue claims do not depend on them.

records.area: Martingale, betting, prediction and selection-rule characterizations
records.scope: Monotone martingales, computable/lower-semicomputable betting, non-monotone Kolmogorov-Loveland strategies, selection rules and unpredictability paradigms.
records.why_it_matters: Provides the unpredictability axis and reveals where adaptive/non-monotonic access changes a randomness notion.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S002 now has primary statement-level computable-martingale, Schnorr bounded-rate martingale and Kurtz weak-martingale formulations, but several historical martingale sources and nonmonotone/KL machinery remain uninspected beyond existing records.
next_actions: Acquire remaining historical martingale characterization sources and deepen KL/nonmonotonic machinery; preserve exact success/rate conventions.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Betting/selection paradigms are represented with statement-level computable/Schnorr/Kurtz martingale resources. KL randomness remains abstract-level and should be re-inspected before any future discovery claim turns on its exact non-monotonic strategy convention.

records.area: Kolmogorov complexity, algorithmic information and incompressibility
records.scope: Plain and prefix-free complexity; coding/incompressibility characterizations; finite-string and infinite-sequence interfaces.
records.why_it_matters: Complexity provides a second foundational characterization axis and is central to lowness, dimension and random-real theory.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Kolmogorov 1965 primary text only metadata-inspected.
Primary Levin/Schnorr sources for the prefix-free characterization have not yet been separately catalogued.

P1-S007 adds statement-level self-delimiting H/K evidence connecting finite-string complexity to the quantified initial-segment characterization of infinite-sequence Martin-Löf randomness; no broader complexity-family survey was opened.
next_actions: Inspect primary complexity definitions and original incompressibility-characterization sources; add conditional/monotone variants only where randomness-relevant.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Plain/prefix-free complexity and the finite-string/infinite-sequence interface are source-grounded. Kolmogorov 1965 and selected early Chaitin/Levin/Schnorr originals remain provenance improvements rather than missing support for current definitions.

records.scope: Constructive/effective Hausdorff dimension, supergales, complexity-rate characterizations and finite-string dimension.
records.why_it_matters: Quantifies degrees of algorithmic information/randomness rather than only binary pass/fail notions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Exact supergale definition not statement-inspected, so no DEF record yet.
next_actions: Inspect primary definitions and distinguish constructive dimension, strong dimension and resource-bounded variants.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Constructive/effective dimension is discoverable through stable sources and theorem records, but the exact supergale definition and complexity characterization are still only abstract-level. Any Phase-2 use that depends materially on dimension must first upgrade those statements.

records.scope: Relativized tests/complexity/betting notions; oracle dependence; van Lambalgen-type phenomena; relative random reals.
records.why_it_matters: Relativization is structurally central to lowness, bases, jumps and higher notions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Oracle-relative Martin-Löf, computable, Schnorr and Kurtz notions are now normalized at statement level for the inspected fair-coin Cantor/martingale-test conventions.
The original van Lambalgen 1990 paper is statement-inspected in its actual recursive-sequential-test/product-space notation; the clean modern A⊕B theorem is separately supported by SRC-0030/SRC-0032.
The incoming association of the central theorem with SRC-0020 (a different 1987 van Lambalgen paper) was corrected; see FL-005.

Uniform-versus-ordinary relativization is explicit for Schnorr/computable randomness. Arbitrary measures/spaces and a primary inspection of the original Merkle et al. counterexamples were not pursued in this bounded session.
next_actions: Later extend relativization beyond fair-coin Cantor space with exact measure/representation hypotheses.

If needed for the global relation graph, inspect the original counterexample paper behind failure of naive van-Lambalgen directions for ordinary Schnorr/computable randomness; do not infer it from definitions.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Ordinary versus uniform oracle relativization and van Lambalgen-type results are statement-grounded. Uninspected counterexample originals and arbitrary-measure relativization are outside the required Phase-1 depth.

records.area: Lowness notions and bases for randomness
records.scope: Low-for-randomness classes, K-triviality, bases for randomness, traceability interfaces and computational weakness.
records.why_it_matters: Shows how oracles interact with randomness and supplies equivalence classes connecting complexity and relative randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S012 upgrades SRC-0009 to statement-inspected primary support for exact K-triviality, low-for-Martin-Löf-randomness and low-for-K definitions, plus the source theorem chain proving that all three classes coincide.

SRC-0010 is re-inspected at Definition 1.2 and Theorem 2.1/related statements: base for 1-randomness is kept definitionally distinct from lowness, and bases for 1-randomness are exactly the K-trivial sets.

SRC-0021 (Kučera-Terwijn 1999) remains ABSTRACT_INSPECTED: Cambridge internal text was access-restricted and the ILLC archive full-text object was returned as an unsupported gzip payload. Its internal theorem syntax is not reconstructed from later papers.
Low for K is now an explicit finite-string prefix-free-complexity node; it is not conflated with K-triviality or low for randomness before theorem-level equivalences are applied.
Nies's exact theorem that every oracle low for computable randomness is computable was inspected as a bounded contrast, but P1-S012 does not open a Schnorr/computable-lowness survey.

Cost functions, traceability, jump-theoretic characterizations and degree closure were deliberately not expanded: they are not required to complete the principal low-ML/K-trivial/base equivalence package in this bounded pass.
next_actions: Treat COV-0009 as structurally partial rather than complete. Revisit only if the Phase-1 completion audit identifies a specific gate-relevant provenance or terminology gap.
Do not launch a general traceability/cost-function/degree survey merely because those notions occur near K-triviality.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Low for ML randomness, low for K, K-triviality and base for randomness are distinct definitions joined only by inspected theorem records. Kučera-Terwijn 1999 internals remain inaccessible but later primary sources fully support the current equivalence package.

records.scope: 2-randomness, n-randomness, weak-2 comparisons, Demuth randomness and other stronger effective-test notions.
records.why_it_matters: Tests the effect of stronger resources and is necessary for an honest implication/separation map.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S004 now has statement-level primary definitions for Demuth, difference, balanced and Oberwolfach randomness, together with the existing weak-n and jump-based n-randomness records.

Demuth's 1982 original was recovered and inspected, but it is Russian and uses historical constructive notation restricted to arithmetical reals; the modern all-real normal form is cross-checked through SRC-0016/SRC-0035 rather than presented as a verbatim translation.
The source-specific distinction between Demuth's Solovay passing and the ordinary weak-Demuth passing used for balanced/Oberwolfach tests is now explicit.
Relations to arbitrary computable measures/spaces, broader weak/partial Demuth variants and higher-randomness analogues remain outside this bounded tranche.
next_actions: Retain this stratum as partial until broader stronger-test variants and any generalized-measure/higher cross-links needed for Gate 1 are inspected; do not infer missing arrows from the current definitions.
If historical priority details become decision-relevant, obtain an independent translation/secondary philological check for the 1982 Demuth notation rather than guessing from the scan.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: The stronger-test hierarchy is statement-grounded with the Demuth original plus modern primary normalization. The Demuth translation qualification remains explicit and is not a gate blocker.

records.scope: Δ1_1-, Π1_1-Martin-Löf-, Π1_1-randomness, higher weak-2/difference notions and lowness at higher levels.
records.why_it_matters: Tests which classical randomness structures persist under higher computability and where genuinely different phenomena arise.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: SRC-0017 remains ABSTRACT_INSPECTED because the Cambridge chapter full text was not obtained; no exact definition is promoted from it.
Exact higher definitions/comparisons are instead grounded in statement-inspected primary SRC-0052 through SRC-0055.
Early historical Martin-Löf/Sacks formulations are not independently statement-inspected in P1-S009; later primary sources are used to normalize the terminology with provenance explicitly retained.
next_actions: Retain COV-0011 at PARTIAL rather than complete: only deepen higher lowness/stronger-test variants if a later Gate-1 coverage audit identifies a concrete need.
Preserve DEF-0020 as the finite n-randomness convention and keep continuous higher relativization separate from ordinary oracle relativization.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Principal higher-randomness definitions and strict comparisons are statement-grounded in later primary literature. Earlier Martin-Löf/Sacks originals remain historical navigation gaps and are not used to reconstruct unavailable syntax.

records.scope: Preservation under effective measure-preserving maps; existence of random preimages; notion-specific failures and maximality principles.
records.why_it_matters: Supplies structural invariance principles that can distinguish randomness notions independently of their syntactic definitions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S005 upgrades SRC-0015 to statement level and records exact a.e.-computable map hypotheses for computable-randomness NRFN, Schnorr NRFN failure, fair-coin and all-computable-measure ML maximality, plus primary conservation/isomorphism statements from SRC-0011/SRC-0012.

The historical Shen antecedent for Martin-Löf no-randomness-from-nothing was not independently recovered as an original standalone source; the exact modern statements are preserved from inspected primary papers.
No global conservation/NRFN table beyond the exact notions needed for this session is promoted; fair-coin stronger-randomness records from P1-S004 remain scoped as before.
next_actions: Only if needed for Gate-1 completeness, trace the earliest standalone Martin-Löf NRFN provenance and any remaining exact map-class variants without reopening a broad stronger-randomness survey.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Conservation/NRFN statements and notion-specific failures are statement-grounded. Earliest standalone Martin-Löf no-randomness-from-nothing provenance remains unresolved but does not affect exact modern claims.

records.area: Computable probability spaces and randomness beyond Cantor space
records.scope: Computable metric/probability spaces, arbitrary computable measures, uniform tests, isomorphisms and non-binary domains.
records.why_it_matters: Prevents the programme from mistaking Cantor-space presentation choices for intrinsic features of randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S005 now has statement-level primary definitions for computable metric/probability spaces, generalized Martin-Löf and Schnorr tests, measure-parameter uniform tests, morphisms/isomorphisms, binary representations, the atomless Lebesgue-space theorem, and exact conservation/invariance links.
The general Cantor representation uses an appropriate computable measure, not automatically fair coin. Atomlessness is required for the stronger fixed nonatomic/Lebesgue model.
Arbitrary represented-space formalisms beyond the inspected computable-metric-space setting remain uninspected; no theorem is inferred for them by analogy.
next_actions: A later coverage audit should decide whether the current primary computable-metric-space stratum is sufficient for Gate 1 or whether one bounded represented-space source is still needed.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Computable metric/probability spaces, representations, morphisms and generalized tests are statement-grounded. More general represented-space formalisms are deliberately outside scope.

records.scope: Typicality, effective ergodic theorems, mixing computable dynamics and probability-theoretic characterizations tied to individual randomness.
records.why_it_matters: Connects individual randomness to long-run statistical behavior under dynamical systems.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: The final author-hosted Franklin-Towsner PDF timed out in P1-S010; exact theorem statements promoted here come from the inspected arXiv copy, while journal/DOI metadata establish the publication identity. Theorem numbering is therefore copy-qualified.

Franklin-Greenberg-Miller-Ng (2012) was located bibliographically and at abstract level, but a full primary copy was not statement-inspected in this bounded pass; no theorem record is reconstructed from its abstract.

COV-0014 remains PARTIAL: the principal Martin-Löf/Schnorr/weak-2 effective-Birkhoff interfaces are now statement-grounded, but this was not a general ergodic-theory, recurrence, or computable-analysis survey.
next_actions: Retain COV-0014 at PARTIAL unless a later Gate-1 coverage audit identifies a concrete remaining ergodic-interface gap; do not expand into a general dynamics survey.
If the Franklin-Greenberg-Miller-Ng effectively-closed-set theorem becomes necessary for Gate-1 completeness, obtain full statement-level primary access before promotion.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: The principal effective-Birkhoff interfaces are statement-grounded with hypotheses preserved. Franklin-Greenberg-Miller-Ng remains abstract-level, but no promoted theorem depends on its uninspected internal statement.

records.area: Finite strings, random reals, left-c.e. reals and Ω
records.scope: Randomness/patternlessness for finite strings; infinite reals as binary sequences; left-c.e. random reals; Chaitin Ω and related representations.
records.why_it_matters: Clarifies object type and prevents conflating finite incompressibility with infinite-sequence randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S007 now has statement-level primary coverage for the finite-string/infinite-sequence self-delimiting-complexity distinction, left-c.e. (historical r.e.) reals, prefix-free halting probabilities, Chaitin Ω-numbers, and the exact random-left-c.e./Ω characterization.

SRC-0045 was statement-inspected through Chaitin's collected-paper reprint after bibliographic identity was cross-checked against IBM/DOI metadata. SRC-0004 remains ABSTRACT_INSPECTED; the 1966 source is not silently upgraded and the distinct 1969 continuation remains separate under the FL-002 title correction history.
The Solovay draft cited by the 2001 primary papers was not independently recovered at statement level in this bounded pass; no theorem detail is promoted from the inaccessible manuscript.
The 2001 primary sources use 'recursively enumerable real'; P1-S007 normalizes this to the modern alias 'left-c.e. real' while preserving the source vocabulary and one-sided approximation definition.
No arbitrary left-c.e. real is identified as random. Universality is kept explicit whenever Martin-Löf randomness of a halting probability is asserted.
No relative-Ω/oracle survey, generalized-measure transfer, stronger-test transfer or category analogy was opened.
next_actions: If later Phase-1 completeness requires historical provenance beyond the present statement-level core, inspect the 1966/1969 Chaitin internals and the Solovay draft if accessible; otherwise preserve their access gaps explicitly.
Keep future Ω additions hypothesis-exact: distinguish arbitrary prefix-free halting probabilities from universal-machine Ω-numbers and preserve binary-representation conventions.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Finite-string versus infinite-sequence distinctions, left-c.e. reals and Ω are statement-grounded. Selected early Chaitin originals and the Solovay draft remain provenance/history improvements only.

records.area: Pseudorandomness, resource-bounded randomness and derandomization boundary
records.scope: Computational indistinguishability, resource-bounded betting/measure/dimension and derandomization only to clarify contrast with 'genuine' individual randomness.
records.why_it_matters: Needed to distinguish algorithmic randomness of individuals from bounded-observer pseudorandomness without allowing Phase 1 to drift into general complexity theory.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Yao 1982 statement inspection used an accessible scan matched to DOI/proceedings metadata rather than relying on the access-limited IEEE landing page.
HILL 1999 statement inspection used an author-hosted full journal paper matched to SIAM metadata.
Nisan-Wigderson statement inspection used the author-hosted 1988 FOCS extended abstract plus 1994 journal metadata/abstract; exact journal theorem numbering was not inferred.
The bounded pass deliberately does not survey cryptographic PRG variants, resource-bounded dimensions, or derandomization beyond the object/resource boundary needed by this catalogue.
next_actions: Boundary objective satisfied for P1-S008 at partial depth: preserve the ensemble/individual-sequence/language-characteristic-sequence distinctions and the attached resource bounds.
Do not expand this stratum into a general cryptography or complexity-theory survey unless later Gate-1 review identifies a concrete catalogue gap.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: The intended boundary is met: computational pseudorandomness, resource-bounded individual randomness and derandomization are separated. Resource-bounded dimension and broader cryptographic/complexity variants are deliberately omitted.

records.scope: Chance vs individual randomness; statistical typicality vs unpredictability vs incompressibility; only arguments that materially shape mathematical definitions.
records.why_it_matters: Provides conceptual provenance for why different formal frameworks exist, while avoiding nontechnical philosophical sprawl.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: No dedicated philosophy-of-probability literature was collected because P1-S001 prioritizes mathematical definitions/results.
next_actions: Add only sources that resolve terminology/provenance or materially explain formal design choices.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: The mathematical boundary among typicality, unpredictability and incompressibility is represented. A general philosophy-of-probability survey is intentionally outside Phase-1 discovery-library depth.

records.scope: Implications, strict implications, equivalences, incomparabilities, relativized relationships and known separations among indexed notions.
records.why_it_matters: A future agent must be able to traverse what a notion implies and what implies it without guessing from definitions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S005 adds exact generalized-measure/space edges for Martin-Löf and Schnorr conservation, computable-randomness NRFN and isomorphism invariance, Schnorr NRFN failure, computable Cantor representations, the atomless Lebesgue reduction, and separate fair-coin versus all-computable-measure ML maximality.

The global graph remains incomplete across higher randomness, category-adjacent notions and several characterization families; no uninspected transitive, converse or fair-coin-to-general-measure edge is promoted.

P1-S007 adds exact edges separating arbitrary prefix-free halting probabilities, left-c.e. reals, universal Ω-numbers and Martin-Löf-random left-c.e. reals; no converse or universality claim is inferred beyond THM-0047/THM-0048.

P1-S011 adds exact fair-coin formulation-equivalence, Solovay-test and c.e.-martingale characterization edges for Martin-Löf randomness. The ordinary finite-sum Solovay test is kept distinct from the Schnorr total-Solovay convention, and lower-semicomputable martingales are kept distinct from computable martingales.

P1-S012 adds the principal lowness/base equivalence triangle at statement level: low for Martin-Löf randomness ↔ low for K ↔ K-triviality, plus base for 1-randomness ↔ K-triviality. Definitions are kept separate and no closure/transitive edge outside the inspected theorem package is inferred.
next_actions: During the Phase-1 completion audit, test the cross-cutting graph for consequential missing primary provenance or hypotheses before deepening any already-partial stratum.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: The relationship map contains inspected implications/equivalences/separations and explicitly avoids inferred converses or transitive edges. Exhaustive closure of the global graph is not required for Gate 1.

records.area: Effective category, genericity and non-measure alternative frameworks
records.scope: Category-based smallness/genericity and other mathematically established alternatives that illuminate the boundary of 'randomness' versus genericity.
records.why_it_matters: The project charter includes measure/category interfaces; understanding nearby non-measure notions prevents conflation of randomness and genericity.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S006 now has statement-level primary definitions for effective meagreness, weak 1-genericity, 1-genericity, weak n-genericity and n-genericity, together with the strict weak-1-generic → Kurtz-random bridge and the interleaving genericity hierarchy.

Jockusch's 1980 foundational chapter remains METADATA_ONLY internally, and Kurtz's 1983 original weak-genericity paper is available only through its publisher extract in this repository pass. Exact syntax is therefore grounded in later statement-inspected primary papers rather than reconstructed from inaccessible originals.
Kurtz's 1981 thesis SRC-0025 remains METADATA_ONLY. P1-S006 did not manufacture original priority detail from the thesis.

No probability-measure consequence is inferred merely from category definitions, and no category consequence is inferred merely from measure-null definitions. The only cross-framework implication added is the exact primary statement REL-0037.

The session did not expand into general forcing, oracle-genericity, computable-metric-space genericity, or higher-category surveys beyond the definitions and hierarchy needed to keep weak/1/higher genericity distinct.
next_actions: If accessible in a later Phase-1 retrieval pass, inspect the internal statements of Jockusch 1980, Kurtz 1981 and Kurtz 1983; otherwise preserve their present access levels.
Do not broaden COV-0019 by analogy: add further category/randomness comparisons only when an exact primary statement is inspected.

p1_s013_audit.rationale: Effective category/genericity definitions and the bounded bridge to Kurtz randomness are statement-grounded in later primary sources. Jockusch/Kurtz originals remain historical provenance gaps only.

audit_summary.note: All 19 strata remain PARTIAL depth tags. P1-S013 separately records that their present depth is sufficient for a formal Gate-1 review; this is not a Gate-1 PASS and does not assert exhaustive literature coverage.
